scope: Proposition 3.2 (A tournament for probabilistic comparisons) of the manuscript “A Nearly Quartic Separation Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity” (preprints/A-Nearly-Quartic-Separation-Between-Randomized-and-Quantum-Query-Complexity-October-5-2026/quartic-query-separation.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 284 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a99f1c38d086a335), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For m ≥ 2, put T = ⌈log(1000m)⌉, ϵ = 1 1000T . Suppose a coherent comparison circuit, controlled by two candidate indices and reversible with all workspace retained, uses at most c ≥ 1 bit queries. Let aij be the probability that it reports i defeating j, and assume (10). There is a quantum algorithm making O c √ m T2 log T  queries on every branch and returning a list of at most T candidates with the following guarantee. If i∗ ∈ [m] satisfies ai∗j ≥ 1 − ϵ (j ̸= i∗), (11) then the list contains i∗ with probability at least 1 − 2m/2T − Tϵ.
